content:
The image shows an opened soybean pod with two seeds inside. Key observations:

- The pod wall has brown/rusty discoloration and streaking on its inner surface
- There is white fluffy/cottony material visible at the base of the pod (bottom of the image)
- The seeds themselves appear green/yellow and relatively normal in shape
- The pod interior shows some browning and what appears to be mycelial growth

The white cottony material inside the pod is a strong indicator of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot). The description states: "pods contain smaller, lighter, cottony seeds" and "infected seeds may be flat, shriveled, or replaced by sclerotia." The white fluffy material at the pod base is consistent with white mold mycelium inside the pod.

However, looking more carefully, the white material could also be the natural pod membrane. The brown streaking on the pod wall is notable. 

Reconsidering: the brown discoloration on the pod wall with the white material inside aligns most closely with White Mold, which causes bleached white pods with white fluffy mycelial growth inside pods and black sclerotia.
